key_insight: Lunar tides can resonantly drive flow in Earth’s liquid core when a basal magma ocean separates the core from the mantle, creating a new tidal-coupling mechanism distinct from classical boundary-forced tides.
engineering_relevance: The theory helps estimate when resonant tidal forcing could amplify core flow, magnetic Reynolds number, and instability, offering a new geodynamo-relevant mechanism for differentiated planetary interiors.
method: Developed an inviscid theory for a two-fluid core–BMO system with tidal forcing acting on the density interface.
Showed a transition from equilibrium tide to inertia–self-gravity wave response, with a resonance at the interfacial natural frequency.
Added finite-viscosity effects and coupled the model to lunar recession and BMO crystallisation parameterisations.
evidence_signal: The paper presents analytical/theoretical predictions rather than direct experimental or simulation data, using parameterised evolutionary models to estimate tidal response and instability metrics.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on idealised two-layer fluid assumptions and parameterised histories for lunar recession and BMO evolution, so real planetary stratification and dissipation may shift the resonance.
paper_title: Resonant lunar tides of Earth's core and basal magma ocean
